title: Config Guardian: Safety Arbiter for Cost-driven Config Changes and State Reconciliation
creator: Aisha Romero
description:
Problem: Config changes that tweak batching, caching, or routing policies can have outsized cost or latency impacts when applied at scale. We need an automated safety layer that evaluates proposed config updates, simulates downstream effects on batching/caching efficiency and unit cost, and prevents blind rollouts that could regress SLOs or spike costs.

Goal: Build a Config Guardian service that acts as an arbiter during config apply flows: it runs a lightweight simulation against recent traffic patterns, enforces guardrails (cost delta, p50/p95 latency thresholds, cache hit-rate regression), creates a reconciliation plan for divergent state, and automatically triggers safe mitigations (canary hold, staged apply with hysteresis, or orchestrated revert) when thresholds are breached.

Scope:
- Input surface: config changes submitted via Console, API, or infra pipelines that affect batching, KV cache policies, quantization selection, and routing overrides.
- Enforcer features: pre-apply simulation, risk score, staged rollouts (percent-based), silent canary shadowing, live comparison against baseline metrics, and automated safe-hold/revert actions.
- Reconciliation: maintain a minimal drift ledger and state harmonizer that can detect partial failures (e.g., half the fleet applied, older control-plane state) and reconcile to a known-good state or run a coordinated rollback.
- Observability: decision trace for each apply (sim params, snapshots, risk score), actionable alerts, and cost impact estimates.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Config Guardian evaluates >90% of config change types in preflight, returns a risk score and simulation summary within 10s for typical apply payloads.
2) Automatic canary/stage rollout machinery supports percent-based gating and hysteresis with a default safe policy.
3) Automatic mitigations trigger when simulated or live metrics cross configured thresholds; mitigations include pause, rollback-to-snapshot, or switch to fallback model variant.
4) Reconciliation component can detect and resolve split-brain apply states for a region within 5 minutes using an idempotent apply plan.
5) Console surfaces decision logs, estimated cost delta, and links to the simulation artifact and PR.

Trade-offs and design notes:
- Simulation fidelity vs latency: we will start with a deterministic traffic-sampling simulator (replay recent 5 minutes of prefix classes) to estimate batching and cache behavior; higher-fidelity blackbox simulations are future work.
- Safety-first defaults: conservative thresholds to avoid customer-facing regressions; teams can opt-in to relaxed policies per project.
- Integration points: hooks into rollout engine (existing autoscaling/router), traces to APM, and cost analytics for unit-cost extrapolation.

Non-goals: full offline re-sim of long-tail traffic, replacing manual SRE approvals for high-risk enterprise-only changes (those can opt into manual gating).
updates: 2026-02-26: Kickoff meeting with runtime, platform, and DX. Drafted initial ADR and confluence page: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Config+Guardian+Design

2026-03-03: Prototype simulator implemented in runtime test harness; can replay sampling of recent requests and estimate effective batch size and cache hits. Benchmark: ~7s for 5k sampled requests on staging cluster.
2026-03-05: Design review with Product and Security. Agreed on default guardrail values and explicit opt-out path for Dedicated customers. Action: add KMS audit entry for auto-reverts.
2026-03-08: PoC PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5482 — includes simulation hook and decision-trace schema. Requesting reviewers: @maria-gonzalez, @kyle-wu.

2026-03-10: Integration smoke run in staging with a batching change that reduced batch size; Config Guardian flagged risk (estimated +18% token cost, p95 latency +12%) and blocked rollout. Follow-up: tune simulation sampling weight for tail prefixes.

2026-03-12: Implemented reconciliation ledger to track apply transaction IDs and partial-applies; added a reconciler job that can run idempotent roll-forward or roll-back plans. Running longer soak tests this week.
next_steps: Complete unit and integration tests for simulation accuracy (target: mean error <5% on cost estimate)
Add canary-stage hooks to rollout engine and expose per-project policy in Console
Deliver operator runbook for manually forcing revert or approving blocked applies
